1.title: RBI Customer Liability & Zero-Liability Protection for Unauthorized Electronic Payment Transactions — Section 2.2 Compliance Annex (DOC_RBI_001)
1.text: [DOC_RBI_001 | rbi | RBI/DBR/2017-18/15-DPSS.CO.PD/Section 2.2 | R01_NEW_DEVICE] Document ID: DOC_RBI_001 | Category: RBI Regulatory Directive | Reference: RBI/DBR/2017-18/15-DPSS.CO.PD/Section 2.2 | Primary Signal: R01_NEW_DEVICE. Under the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Master Direction on Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions, a customer's financial liability is strictly zero when an unauthorized transaction occurs due to contributory fraud, negligence, or security deficiency on the part of the payment aggregator or bank, irrespective of whether the transaction is reported by the customer. Furthermore, third-party breach incidents where the deficiency lies neither with the regulated entity nor with the customer, but elsewhere in the payment ecosystem, also qualify for zero customer liability provided the customer notifies the payment service provider within three working days of receiving the transaction communication alert. When a customer reports an unauthorized UPI, card, wallet, or net-banking debit between four and seven working days after receiving the SMS or email notification, the maximum customer liability is capped at Rs. 10,000 for basic savings and prepaid accounts or Rs. 25,000 for standard current and credit accounts. 2.title: RBI Customer Liability & Zero-Liability Protection for Unauthorized Electronic Payment Transactions — Section 2.2 Compliance Annex (DOC_RBI_001)

Upon receipt of any unauthorized transaction report, the regulated entity must credit the disputed amount back to the customer's account (shadow reversal) within ten working days (T+10 SLA) from the date of notification, without waiting for insurance settlement or final chargeback adjudication. The burden of proving customer liability or intentional credential sharing rests exclusively on the payment aggregator and issuing bank through verifiable device telemetry, AFA logs, and cryptographic device-binding records. Operational Compliance Note (Section 2.2, Regional Audit Zone: Mumbai): Payment aggregator compliance officers and automated RAG explanation services must cite RBI/DBR/2017-18/15-DPSS.CO.PD (Section 2.2) whenever adjudicating disputes involving R01_NEW_DEVICE. 7.title: RBI Guidelines on Regulation of Payment Aggregators (PA/PG) Merchant Onboarding & Escrow Governance — Section 5.5 Compliance Annex (DOC_RBI_004)
7.text: [DOC_RBI_004 | rbi | RBI/DPSS/2020-21/PA-PG-18/Section 5.5 | R08_HIGH_RISK_MCC] Document ID: DOC_RBI_004 | Category: RBI Regulatory Directive | Reference: RBI/DPSS/2020-21/PA-PG-18/Section 5.5 | Primary Signal: R08_HIGH_RISK_MCC. Under the RBI Framework for Regulation of Payment Aggregators and Payment Gateways, non-bank payment aggregators must execute comprehensive merchant due diligence, background screening, and continuous transaction monitoring across all onboarded merchant terminals (`merchant_id`). Merchants operating in elevated chargeback or money-laundering exposure categories—specifically online real-money gaming (`gaming`), digital gift cards (`gift_cards`), virtual digital assets (`crypto`), high-value consumer electronics (`electronics`), and last-minute travel ticketing (`travel`), tracked under reason code `R08_HIGH_RISK_MCC`—are subject to enhanced KYC verification, website security audits, and stricter rolling settlement holds. All funds collected from customers must be credited into an escrow account maintained with a scheduled commercial bank on a strictly T+0 or T+1 basis. Payment aggregators are prohibited from onboarding unregistered offshore gaming or unauthorized crypto exchanges and must continuously monitor merchant-level target-encoded fraud rates (`FE-08 mcc_target_encoded_rate`). If a merchant terminal receives payments from shared devices utilized by two or more distinct customer accounts within a seven-day window (`FE-09`), merchant payout settlement must be paused pending forensic graph review. The RBI Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs) and Digital Account Onboarding establishes tiered transaction limits and mandatory velocity controls for newly opened or recently upgraded customer accounts (`account_age < 30` days, reason code `R06_NEW_ACCOUNT`). 187.title: IST Timezone Normalization Policy (`UTC+05:30`) for Nocturnal Fraud Window Detection (`FE-04` / `R03_ODD_HOUR`) (POL-TIME-004 v2.5 — DOC_POL_004)

Internal Feature Standardization Policy `POL-TIME-004` resolves a critical timezone bug observed in legacy fraud rule engines. While all raw transaction timestamps (`transaction_time`, `outcome_time`, `feature_as_of`) are persisted in Coordinated Universal Time (`UTC`) across PostgreSQL and MongoDB, customer behavioral sleep cycles across Indian cities (Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad) follow Indian Standard Time (`IST = UTC + 05:30`). Evaluating `hour_of_day` in raw UTC misclassifies prime Indian morning shopping hours (`05:30` to `10:29` IST, which corresponds to `00:00` to `04:59` UTC) as nocturnal activity, inflating false positives by over 40%. 207.title: IST Timezone Normalization Policy (`UTC+05:30`) for Nocturnal Fraud Window Detection (`FE-04` / `R03_ODD_HOUR`) (POL-TIME-004 v2.3 — DOC_POL_014)
207.text: [DOC_POL_014 | internal_policies | POL-TIME-004-v2.3 | R03_ODD_HOUR] Document ID: DOC_POL_014 | Category: Internal Risk & Architecture Policy | Policy Code: POL-TIME-004 (v2.3) | Primary Signal: R03_ODD_HOUR. Internal Feature Standardization Policy `POL-TIME-004` resolves a critical timezone bug observed in legacy fraud rule engines. While all raw transaction timestamps (`transaction_time`, `outcome_time`, `feature_as_of`) are persisted in Coordinated Universal Time (`UTC`) across PostgreSQL and MongoDB, customer behavioral sleep cycles across Indian cities (Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad) follow Indian Standard Time (`IST = UTC + 05:30`). Evaluating `hour_of_day` in raw UTC misclassifies prime Indian morning shopping hours (`05:30` to `10:29` IST, which corresponds to `00:00` to `04:59` UTC) as nocturnal activity, inflating false positives by over 40%. All batch feature scripts and real-time online scoring workers must validate IST parity against reference `features` snapshots prior to deployment. Evaluating `hour_of_day` in raw UTC misclassifies prime Indian morning shopping hours (`05:30` to `10:29` IST, which corresponds to `00:00` to `04:59` UTC) as nocturnal activity, inflating false positives by over 40%. Therefore, `FE-04` mandates explicit conversion of `transaction_time` to `UTC+05:30` prior to extracting `hour_of_day` (`0..23`), and sets `is_night = True` (triggering reason code `R03_ODD_HOUR`) if and only if `0 <= hour_of_day_ist < 5` (`00:00:00` through `04:59:59` IST). All batch feature scripts and real-time online scoring workers must validate IST parity against reference `features` snapshots prior to deployment.
